role.altitude: The bioengineer keeps scoping improvements, judging experiment results, deciding specifications and working through problems with scientists and production; typing quotes into estimates, building plans from scratch, compiling issue lists and hunting for data files shrink.
skills_to_grow: Maintaining price tables and plan templates
Checking drafted rationale against result tables
role.ambitious_version: An engineer whose plans and specifications are assembled from records, leaving time for the experiments and the decisions.

tasks.short: Scope the improvement, collect supplier quotes, build the budgetary estimate and timeline, prepare the capital spending request with its justification, and check and submit it.

steps.what: Engineer defines the scope and requirements of the equipment or facility improvement
Engineer requests quotes from suppliers
Engineer enters quote lines into the cost estimate

loop.output: Estimate lines with item, quantity, unit price and delivery time.
loop.check: Line totals must add up to the quote total; the engineer checks each line against the quote.
loop.stop: Quotes whose totals do not reconcile are entered by hand.

steps.what: Engineer builds the budgetary estimates: equipment, installation, validation and contingency
Engineer builds the project timeline: design, purchase, installation and qualification
Engineer fills in the capital spending request form
Engineer writes the justification, benefits and risks of the improvement
Engineer checks the final capital spending request: scope, estimate, timeline and justification
Engineer submits the checked request to the investment committee in the approval workflow

tasks.design: A bounded extraction step reads supplier quotes into estimate lines, with line totals reconciled to each quote total, and the engineer checks each line. The estimate template prices standard cost lines (installation, validation, contingency) from a price table of past orders. A plan template with standard phases and typical durations gives the first timeline for the engineer to adjust. The capital spending request form is pre-filled from the estimate and plan in the approval workflow. Scoping, the justification and the final check stay with the engineer.

approvals.approved_version: The capital spending request with scope, estimate, timeline and justification exactly as checked by the engineer in s8, submitted once to the investment committee in the approval workflow; any change needs a new check.

tasks.previous_blocker: Quotes were typed into spreadsheets and each plan started from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Quote extraction with total checks and estimate and plan templates.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing which improvement will actually pay back.
tasks.altitude: Less typing and building; scoping and arguing the case stay.

reach.learn: Whether requests are complete and comparable.

evidence.claim: Cost estimates are quantities times a price table; a model only reads supplier quotes, checked against totals.

assumptions: Boundary: planning one improvement; managing team budgets and contracts (task 21854) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s4: price table of past orders kept by purchasing, covering about 60% of cost lines; s4 is priced at that share.
Scoping, requesting quotes, the justification and the final check keep their full time.
unknowns: Number of capital requests per year.
research_questions: Are requests prepared faster without larger budget overruns?

incremental.description: Engineer keeps the plan template and price table current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: unusual equipment with few past prices and quotes in odd formats, so s4 keeps 85 and s3 keeps 70 (12.7); high: repeat improvements with known suppliers (19.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Arrange consultations, gather the scientists' data, review it, consult with chemists or biologists to develop or evaluate novel technologies, and record agreed next steps.

steps.what: Engineer arranges consultations with the scientists
Engineer gathers the scientists' data files
Engineer reviews the data and findings
Engineer consults with chemists or biologists to develop or evaluate the novel technology
Engineer records the agreed next steps

tasks.design: A scheduling poll finds meeting times, and a shared project workspace gives the engineer read access to the scientists' data in the electronic lab notebook instead of files sent by mail. Next steps go on the workspace's action list with owners instead of a summary mail. Reviewing the data and the consultation stay with the people.
tasks.previous_blocker: Meetings and data moved by mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Scheduling polls and shared project workspaces.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing which lab result can be scaled and which cannot.

evidence.claim: Shared workspaces and scheduling polls replace mail threads with attachments.

assumptions: Boundary: consulting scientists on new technology; conferring with biomanufacturing on design and production (task 21843) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s2: scientists keep data in the shared lab notebook, for about 60% of projects; s2 is priced at that share.
Reviewing and consulting keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of data in shared notebooks.

incremental.description: Engineer keeps the action list current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly external partners outside the shared workspace, so meetings are still arranged by mail (s1 keeps 80) and data sent as files (s2 keeps 80) (4.8); high: internal teams in one workspace (9.8).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Compile open design and production issues, confer with research and biomanufacturing personnel, check designs against production limits, record decisions, and follow up actions.

steps.what: Research and production staff log design and production issues in the shared tracker: by mail today
Engineer compiles open design and production issues for the meeting
Engineer confers with research and biomanufacturing personnel
Engineer judges the compatibility of design and production limits such as scale, equipment and materials
Engineer records decisions and actions
Engineer follows up open actions

tasks.design: Research and production log design-production issues in one shared issue tracker, so the agenda is a filtered view instead of a list compiled from mails. Decisions and actions are recorded against each issue with owner and due date, and the tracker sends reminders on overdue actions. Conferring and judging compatibility stay with the people.
tasks.previous_blocker: Issues were spread over mails and meeting notes.
tasks.still_hard: Issues raised only in conversation on the floor.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a lab step will not survive at production scale.
tasks.altitude: Less compiling and chasing; conferring stays.

evidence.claim: Spreadsheets and e-mailed review comments glue teams today; product lifecycle systems with document control replace them.

assumptions: Boundary: conferring on design and production; transferring processes to commercial scale (task 21850) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s1: research and production staff log issues in the tracker, for about 70% of issues; s1 is priced at that share.
Conferring, judging and recording decisions keep their full time; recording against the issue instead of in minutes is a first record. Staff logging issues is shown in s6.
unknowns: How many issues are raised outside the tracker.

incremental.description: Engineer keeps issues in the tracker current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: issues are raised mostly in conversation, so the agenda is still compiled from mails and s1 keeps 80 (4.5); high: about 70% of issues logged in the tracker (8.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Pull bench and pilot results, analyse them against process objectives, decide and recommend process formulas, instrumentation or equipment specifications, write the recommendation, and check and sign it.

steps.what: Engineer compiles results of bench and pilot runs
Engineer analyses the results against process objectives
Engineer decides the process formulas, instrumentation or equipment specifications to recommend
Engineer writes the recommendation and specification document

loop.input: The chosen parameters, result tables and the specification template.
loop.output: A specification filled from the parameters and a draft rationale.
loop.check: Every number in the text must match a result table or chosen parameter; the engineer checks that the rationale states why each parameter was chosen as the engineer decided, and rewrites it.
loop.stop: The engineer keeps the draft, or writes it by hand after two redrafts.
loop.why_not_simpler: The rationale differs per process and experiment.

steps.what: Engineer checks and signs the final recommendation

tasks.design: Run results come from the experiment database as tables per run and condition, instead of being copied from run files into a spreadsheet. Analysing and choosing the parameters stay with the engineer. The specification template is filled from the chosen parameters, and a drafting step writes a first rationale in which every number must match a result table; the engineer rewrites and signs it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Results were copied by hand and specifications written from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Experiment databases and templates filled from records.
tasks.still_hard: Pilot runs whose data sit in instrument files only.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing a specification production can actually hold.
tasks.altitude: Less copying and typing; judgement stays.

evidence.claim: In a writing experiment with 453 professionals, not engineers, a model cut time by 40% and raised quality by 18%.
GMP Annex 11 governs computerised systems used in pharmaceutical manufacturing.

assumptions: Boundary: recommending from experiments; maintaining experiment databases (task 21853) and preparing reports for publication or regulators (task 21856) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s1: run results kept in the experiment database by sibling task 21853, for about 70% of runs; s1 is priced at that share.
Analysing, deciding and signing keep their full time.
s4 keeps 70: the specification fields fill from the chosen parameters, but the rationale is rewritten by the engineer.
unknowns: Share of pilot data in the experiment database.
research_questions: Are specifications issued sooner without more errors?

incremental.description: Engineer keeps the specification template current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: data mostly in instrument files, so results are still copied (s1 keeps 80), and the rationale is written from scratch (s4 keeps 85) (6.5); high: data in the database and standard templates (15.5).
